question.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}64{x}^{2}+25 & =0 \\ 64{x}^{2} & =-25 \\ {x}^{2} & =-\frac{25}{64}\end{aligned}
$$

By taking square root, we obtain:

$$
x=\pm \sqrt{-\frac{25}{64}}
$$

We now rewrite $x$ using the imaginary unit $\text{i}=\sqrt{-1}\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\pm \sqrt{-\frac{25}{64}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{25}{64}\cdot (-1)} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{25}{64}}\cdot \sqrt{-1} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{25}}{\sqrt{64}}\cdot \sqrt{-1} \\  & =\pm \frac{5}{8}\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$
